02 / The complete request journey

Keep the existing sequence. Make each step easy to understand and easy to return to.

These are HTML mockups, not screenshots. Buttons, disclosures, input fields and native dialogs work. Values are illustrative. A completed mock interaction is not evidence of a blockchain transaction.

STEP 01

Choose the LP amount

Use a 16 px minimum input text size; show a large amount and a clear premium summary. Keep LP details available without making the default sheet long.

STEP 02

Review the creation request

Keep the approved Claim $X label, green reward amount and Back action. Make the separate $2 ETH fee legible above the primary action.

STEP 03

Hand off to the wallet

Keep wallet choice explicit. The app must preserve the request, selected account and intended chain when the wallet application takes focus.

STEP 04

Return to C06

Show four verified creation stages. Closing this sheet does not cancel or reset the request. Preserve completed stages through a verification outage.

STEP 05

Confirm the actual LP deposit

Only after full premium funding: refresh quantities, then show the exact wrap/approval/deposit sequence. Each real transaction remains a separate explicit confirmation.

STEP 06

Claim the premium after start

Make claimable premium distinct from the original request action. The LP remains locked until its verified maturity time.

STEP 07

Follow an active position

Show start and maturity together, with an explicit timezone. Keep withdrawal disabled before maturity; a countdown is not authorization.

STEP 08

Withdraw at maturity

Use current ownership and fresh quantities to enable the action. Preserve the completed record after withdrawal. No retirement or refund-request workflow returns.

Transaction rules do not change. Canonical fee verification, exact quote validity, ownership checks, recovery, full premium funding and explicit wallet confirmations stay in the existing hooks/API. The mobile work changes presentation and navigation only.

03 / Home, Portfolio and Live APR

Put the three frequent destinations in the bottom bar. Put the rest in More.

DestinationMobile treatmentPreserve
HomeSingle-line brand header. Concise introduction. Full-card offer hit area. APR first; Duration and TVL side by side.Three preview offers and existing row order. TVL uses Duration typography. No public budget-capacity disclosure.
PortfolioStatus-first request cards, then position value, premium and one contextual action. Separate saved-payment recovery card.API/database source of truth; durable local recovery records; multiple independent paid requests.
Live APRTouch-friendly pool picker; one primary card; comparisons stack beneath it. History stays available in a disclosure/sheet.Independent baselines, canonical routes, up to three comparisons, data-unavailable states and selected-card PNG export.
MoreWallet/network, Saffron pro, Stats, Audits and Community. Campaigns/Administration only when the existing role permits them.Every existing destination. No invented live statistics. External links remain clearly external.
DESTINATION 02

Status first, detail second

Keep action labels contextual: View progress, Deposit, Claim premium, Withdraw or View request. Do not squeeze status and a long pair name into the same line.

DESTINATION 03

Live APR is not campaign APR

Use existing price/fee data and observation semantics. This mockup uses a numeric history strip rather than introducing a new chart library.

Navigation contractKeep one router and one route owner

Bottom-navigation destinations map to the existing Home, Portfolio and Live APR routes. More can be a local navigation sheet; it does not create a second router. Browser Back, direct links, query strings and pool aliases must continue to work.

Leave the desktop sidebar and its approved hover/selected treatment unchanged above the desktop breakpoint. Do not render both a horizontal mobile menu and a fixed bottom bar.

04 / Responsive layout rules

Use the available pane width—not a guessed device name—to choose the layout.

320–599 px

Phone: one content column, four bottom destinations, full-width bottom sheets, two metrics per offer row.

600–1000 px

Tablet/compact pane: keep touch navigation, use two-column cards where the pane permits them, and center sheets at a readable maximum width.

1001 px+

Desktop: retain the current rail and table. Container width still decides whether a card or table fits when the rail changes.

RuleProposalAcceptance gate
Main gutters16 px on phones; 24 px in tablet panes. Avoid a permanent 64 px collapsed rail on narrow screens.No body-level horizontal scroll at 320, 360, 390, 430, 600, 768 and 1000 px.
Offer hierarchyAPR at 28–30 px. Duration and TVL at 20 px with identical font, weight and numeric settings. Labels at 11–12 px.All three fields remain readable with $9,999,999 and a two-digit duration; allow layout changes, not text overlap.
Touch targetsMinimum 44 × 44 CSS px; prefer 48 px for primary actions. Give adjacent controls at least 8 px breathing room.Back, Close, pool selection, recovery and primary actions all meet the target.
NavigationFour labelled destinations; bottom safe-area padding. Content padding includes the navigation height.The final item and focused control are never hidden under the bar.
SheetsUse 100dvh with fallbacks, a maximum readable width and independent header/body/footer areas. Scroll only the body when necessary.Close and the CTA stay reachable on a 320 × 568 viewport and after content/error expansion.
KeyboardInput text at least 16 px. Keep the focused field visible; move the CTA above the visual keyboard. Use visualViewport only if CSS/browser behavior requires it.Verify on real iOS Safari and Android Chrome with the native keyboard, including rotation and wallet return.
Large textRespect browser text zoom. Reflow labels and allow card height to grow; do not scale the whole page down.Manual 200% text/zoom check preserves labels, navigation and every action.

Breakpoints are proposed, not measured performance claims. The implementation should use the existing shell breakpoint as its starting seam, then qualify the resulting pane sizes. The document’s embedded frames approximate content width; browser chrome and OS insets still need device checks.

06 / Recovery and difficult states

Design the interruptions with the same care as the successful path.

RECOVERY

A payment response is missing

A durable payment card remains in Portfolio. Check the original hash/account. Never use an error as a reason to silently submit a second fee.

VERIFICATION

The API is temporarily unavailable

Keep the last known requests visible. Explain the stale state and pause new position actions. Refresh checks the same data; it does not clear it.

StateWhat the user seesWhat must not happen
No wallet / wrong networkA clear Connect or switch-network action in context. The amount and chosen offer remain saved.Discarding the draft, changing the user’s selected account silently, or hiding the intended chain.
Wallet opened, app resumedThe same quote/payment/position action. A pending transaction offers recovery rather than another send.Duplicate fee, duplicated approval/deposit, or “fresh test” behavior on app resume.
Unpaid quote expiredPreserve the entered amount. Offer a fresh unpaid review using the existing fee-quote policy.Pretend the old fee quote is valid indefinitely because the mobile layout hides a countdown.
Payment accepted, creator offlineSaved C06 request with the correct readiness/progress message.Treat signer inactivity as a missing payment or reintroduce C05.
Premium partially fundedShow waiting-for-funding progress; LP entry remains unavailable.Enabling deposit from a local animation or a guessed percentage.
Position transferred / account changedRefresh current bearer ownership and present only the actions available to the current wallet.Grant withdrawal because the wallet originally requested the vault.
Admin near/over targetAdvisory banner only in authenticated admin Portfolio. Paid requests remain possible.Expose private budget figures in Home or a modal; reintroduce a hard quota.
Storage denied / another tab activeUse the existing recovery failure behavior and clear messaging. Maintain a single canonical interpretation of payment evidence.Claim durable browser recovery succeeded when storage failed, or overwrite another payment record.

Product boundaryNo removed workflow comes back

The mobile proposal does not add refund requests, requester retirement, C05, wallet/request quotas, gas-spending records or treasury balance checks. Manual refunds remain outside this frontend. Portfolio must support any number of separately paid requests, with pagination rather than a product cap.

07 / What the current mobile page tells us

The current page works responsively, but it still carries desktop-shaped priorities.

ObservedNavigation and introductory text occupy a large first-screen area

The current shell stacks its brand/navigation region and account controls above the content. The Home introduction remains two paragraphs. At narrow widths, each offer stacks APR, Duration and TVL vertically.

Do: Consolidate the header, move frequent navigation to a bottom bar, shorten the default introduction and group Duration/TVL side by side.

Why: Make the first useful offer and its comparison fields easier to reach without changing any offer economics.

Gate: At a 390 × 844 layout, the proposed first card is visible without scrolling and all three cards require materially less vertical scrolling than the reference. Measure the implementation; do not treat this as an already achieved app result.

ReferenceCurrent 390 px app screenshot

This is the existing deployed layout captured by the previous compiled-browser check. It is evidence for the layout assessment, not a mobile mockup.

ObservedThe modal already has valuable behavior to keep

The current modal has Back, a preserved deposit amount, LP details, clear fee copy and C06 recovery. The proposal changes the container and visual priority, not those contracts.

Do: Add a mobile sheet layout in the existing modal layer, keeping one focus owner and the current state hooks.

Gate: Escape, Back, close/reopen, wallet return and stale-response tests keep working. At 320 px, no action disappears under a keyboard or the bottom bar.

08 / Implementation plan

Deliver in small, reviewable slices. Qualify the mobile shell before changing the request flow.

  1. Navigation and layout seams

    Add a compact mobile header and labelled bottom navigation to the shared shell. Reuse the existing routes. Put secondary destinations into More and keep role checks in their existing owner. Preserve the desktop rail.

    Gate: direct links, Back/Forward, route focus, active labels and APR observation release still pass at phone/tablet/desktop widths.

  2. Home and Portfolio cards

    Use the compact offer composition below the chosen pane width. Keep Duration and TVL typography matched. Add status-first Portfolio grouping and a distinct saved-payment recovery card. Preserve pagination and last-known data.

    Gate: three placeholder rows render; real/API mode does not inherit fake TVL. Long IDs, large values, empty state and admin-only advisory all fit.

  3. Mobile sheet container

    Adapt the shared modal to a bounded sheet with stable header, scrollable content and safe-area-aware action region. Integrate viewport/keyboard behavior. Keep amount → review → wallet → C06 state in the existing hooks.

    Gate: native keyboard and wallet app switching work on iOS and Android; one payment remains one payment through interruption.

  4. Position lifecycle and Live APR

    Apply the same sheet system to LP approvals/deposit, claim and withdrawal. Give Live APR a touch pool picker and stacked comparisons without rewriting its data client or PNG feature.

    Gate: exact fork-checked lifecycle still completes; ownership/maturity/funding guards hold. Pool changes preserve independent observation semantics.

  5. Qualification and rollout

    Run focused browser checks, then real-device checks. Publish a review build first; keep the current desktop and VNC environments intact. Back up static output and update the source ZIP/runbook before release.

    Gate: the mobile acceptance matrix below is complete. Rollback restores static assets without clearing requests, browser recovery records or databases.
Source seamExpected changeKeep untouched

This plan does not assign invented hour estimates. The keyboard/wallet handoff is the main uncertainty and should be qualified early, not left to the final release check.

09 / Acceptance and device matrix

A narrow desktop browser is useful evidence. It is not a substitute for a real wallet on a phone.

Test surfaceCoverageRelease requirement
Automated Chromium320 × 568, 360 × 800, 390 × 844, 430 × 932; tablet 768 × 1024; desktop 1440 × 900.No body overflow, 44 px targets, visible CTA, correct route state, matched TVL/Duration font, persistent draft and recovery.
iOS Safari + mobile walletSafe areas, native decimal keyboard, rotation, larger text, wallet switch and return, browser Back.Record actual device/browser versions and observed results. No duplicate transaction or discarded draft.
Android Chrome + mobile walletVisual viewport resize, system navigation inset, provider handoff, screen lock/resume and network interruption.Same recovery and action reachability gates as iOS.
Keyboard + assistive technologyTab/Shift-Tab, Escape, native disclosures, readable state labels and screen-reader route/dialog announcements.Focus remains visible, trapped only while a modal is open, and restored to a sensible trigger on close.
Backend fixture / forkLost payment callback, multi-request recovery, exact factory simulation, premium funding, LP entry, claim and mature withdrawal.No weakening of canonical fee, funding, ownership or maturity checks. No live funds needed.
Live APR fixturePool picker, three comparisons, route changes, stale/unavailable data and actual PNG pixels.No accidental extra observers, stale baseline reuse or capture of surrounding navigation.
  • TVL is not shown as capacity or sourced from a private planning target.
  • Refresh status and Refresh vaults retain the existing request and never reset a test.
  • Buttons brighten by 15% with a mouse, remain legible on touch, and keep disabled appearance.
  • Opening the keyboard cannot hide Close, the focused input or the next required action.
  • Every user can make multiple independently paid requests; use pagination when needed.
  • Offline status retains evidence and disables only actions that depend on unavailable verification.
  • Mobile treatment does not alter the approved desktop table, sidebar or live APR data source.
  • Exported source, deployed files and documented build mode agree.
Status of these gates: they are implementation acceptance criteria. The HTML document itself is checked for interaction, layout, offline assets and print behavior. It does not certify real-device wallet behavior or an implemented mobile redesign.

10 / Scope, sources and handoff

What is delivered

A complete standalone HTML document with embedded fonts/assets, editable HTML/CSS/JavaScript mockup sources, an interactive prototype, the full flow gallery and an implementation/acceptance plan.

What is not claimed

The proposed mobile layout has not been merged into the app. Prototype payments are not real. OS keyboard behavior, mobile-wallet interoperability and production usability are not certified by these mockups.

Layout evidence is pinned to the existing source commit f80eefffce1f02412f36e960e0e578e6a25af214. The separately requested 15% hover change is a small live-app update. The report’s gold APR/TVL/fee figures are illustrative unless explicitly identified as existing product copy.
